# Azure load balancer

Deploys a Standard or Gateway Azure load balancer with frontend configurations,
backend pools, probes, load-balancing rules, NAT rules, outbound rules and legacy
VMSS NAT pools. Supports diagnostic settings, role assignments, locks, tags,
telemetry and AzAPI controls. Public IPs and NICs are consumer-owned.

See the [default](examples/default), [complete](examples/complete),
[multi-region](examples/multi-region) and [standalone child](examples/child-resources)
examples. Use Terraform >=1.16 and <2.0 with the provider versions declared by
the module; its interfaces dependency requires AzAPI >=2.13.

## Backend membership

`backend_address_pools` is keyed by stable consumer keys. The exported
`backend_address_pool_resource_ids` uses those same keys.

- **NIC is the default**, including an omitted or null `backend_address_type`.
  The module manages pool metadata but never writes NIC membership or replays
  its read-only projection. There is no explicit-member writer or cleanup for
  NIC pools. Pass the pool IDs to the resource/module owning the NIC.
- **IP is opt-in**: set `backend_address_type = "IP"` and configure
  `backend_address_pool_addresses`. This list is authoritative, including an
  empty list to remove the last member.
- **Frontend is explicit** for Global pools. Each member references an actual
  regional LB frontend through
  `load_balancer_frontend_ip_configuration_resource_id`, not an IP literal.
  Use public Standard regional frontends with compatible IP families.
  Global pools cannot have VNet/tunnel settings. Global rules use one pool,
  matching frontend/backend ports and no TCP reset, probes, NAT or outbound rules.

IP and native NIC members require separate pools, although both kinds can
coexist on one LB:

```hcl
backend_address_pools = {
  static = { name = "static", backend_address_type = "IP" }
  nvas   = { name = "nvas" }
}
```

Point explicit addresses at `"static"`; pass the `"nvas"` pool ID to the NIC
owner. Input validation reports explicit addresses targeting NIC pools. It
cannot validate attachments made by another state; the NIC owner must not
attach native NICs to IP pools.

Modes declare ownership, **not an Azure conversion**. Keep populated IP pools
explicitly IP. Clear explicit members before a separately coordinated switch to
NIC; detach native NICs through their owner before switching away from NIC.
Do not switch modes to bypass validation.
See [NIC ownership](docs/nic-membership-ownership.md) and
[explicit-member behavior](docs/ip-member-persistence.md).

## Ownership and updates

The parent LB owns complete frontend, pool metadata, probe, rule, NAT and
outbound collections. It omits member lists and read-only NIC back-references.
Dedicated pool endpoints manage explicit IP/Frontend members through one
coupled exact-PUT action and refreshing updater. Changed explicit pools require
two PUTs; these are not transactional. The stateless action has a fixed
30-minute timeout and no configurable retry/timeouts. Fixed-empty destroy
actions clear explicit members before pool deletion or rename.

Do not combine this root with standalone child modules or another writer to
the same LB collections. Standalone pool/NAT modules are for externally managed
LBs whose owner delegates those collections and preserves them on every parent
write. The root deliberately keeps pool lifecycle with referencing parent rules
to avoid creation cycles; this is a practical composition boundary, not full
independent-submodule composition. See [composition](docs/child-composition.md).

Configured collections are authoritative. Declare all existing objects before
adoption and remove references when removing a target. Null means unspecified,
not a request to clear a server value; empty managed lists express removal.
Map/reference ordering is normalized for stable requests.

AzAPI replaces on name, parent scope and location changes; SKU, tier and edge
zone also have replacement controls. Frontend edits, including private zones,
are submitted as updates, not automatic LB replacement; Azure may reject
unsupported changes. An in-place plan is not a zero-disruption guarantee.
Review zone migrations and other immutable changes separately.

`resource_types` overrides selected APIs. `retry` and `timeouts` configure
supported managed resources, not the stateless action. `ignore_body_changes`
uses body-relative dot paths; ignored configuration is not sent to Azure and
changes take effect only after apply. Do not use ignores to mask convergence
defects. Diagnostic omitted/null/empty entry sets are unspecified; use explicit
category/group/enabled values for managed entries.

Freeze competing writers during adoption. The parent-ID mutex serializes
operations within one provider process, not across states. Remove ReadOnly
locks before updates and deletion-blocking locks before selective replacement.
The full-destroy lock-removal wait is not an update-time unlock.

## Upgrading from v0.5.0

See the [upgrade guide](docs/upgrade-v0.5.0.md) for address mapping and exceptions.

1. Back up protected state and inventory existing names, IDs, properties,
   memberships, assignment GUIDs and extension settings. Keep the released
   AzureRM provider configuration available until state conversion completes.
2. Replace `resource_group_name` with the existing resource group's `parent_id`.
   Keep LB identity, SKU/tier, edge zone, frontend/child names and input keys.
3. Preserve every explicit IP member and set its pool to `"IP"`. Native NIC
   pools use the NIC default without a new input or explicit-member writes.
4. Move PIP creation and its locks, diagnostics and RBAC to a consumer owner
   using captured IDs/names/settings. Pass `public_ip_address_resource_id`.
   Inspect imports for case-only parent-ID replacement before applying.
5. Update diagnostics to canonical `logs`/`metrics` objects, preserving names
   and destinations. Review output consumers: discrete ID maps remain keyed
   by input keys; raw resource outputs are AzAPI-shaped.
6. Configure complete memberships in the NIC owner, then retire
   `backend_address_pool_network_interfaces`. Module-owned nondestructive
   removals forget legacy association bindings without detaching NICs.
7. Review a saved plan. Module-owned moves preserve LB, lock, diagnostics and
   ordinary RBAC identities at the same boundary/key map. RBAC moves preserve
   native GUIDs without caller imports or a migration flag. Only legacy
   delegated assignments with composite `ARM-ID|tenant` state IDs require the
   narrow per-key import exception in the guide.
8. Reject unintended deletion/replacement or lost membership. Apply only the
   inspected plan, verify independent readbacks and normal refreshed no-op
   plans. A code revert/state restore is not an automatic post-apply rollback.

For older pre-release configurations that relied on the former IP default,
explicitly pin existing IP pools to `"IP"` **before** upgrading. Do not let the
new default silently change ownership. Erroneous explicit-member bindings on
native NIC pools require the selective recovery described in the guide; never
send an empty IP list against native NIC references.

## Required Inputs

The following input variables are required:

### <a name="input_frontend_ip_configurations"></a> [frontend\_ip\_configurations](#input\_frontend\_ip\_configurations)

Description: Frontend configurations keyed by stable consumer keys. `name` defaults to frontend-<LB name>; names must be unique.  
Supply one of public\_ip\_address\_resource\_id, public\_ip\_prefix\_resource\_id, or a subnet.  
PIPs are consumer-owned; creation, PIP tags, DNS, DDoS, zones and PIP extension resources belong in that composition.  
Private frontends support frontend\_private\_ip\_address, frontend\_private\_ip\_address\_allocation (Dynamic/Static),  
frontend\_private\_ip\_address\_version (IPv4/IPv6) and frontend\_private\_ip\_subnet\_resource\_id.  
gateway\_load\_balancer\_frontend\_ip\_configuration\_id chains a Gateway LB frontend.  
zones defaults to 1/2/3 for private frontends; ["None"] omits zones. Public frontends inherit PIP zones.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name                                               = optional(string)
    frontend_private_ip_address                        = optional(string)
    frontend_private_ip_address_version                = optional(string, "IPv4")
    frontend_private_ip_address_allocation             = optional(string, "Dynamic")
    frontend_private_ip_subnet_resource_id             = optional(string)
    gateway_load_balancer_frontend_ip_configuration_id = optional(string)
    public_ip_address_resource_id                      = optional(string)
    public_ip_prefix_resource_id                       = optional(string)
    zones                                              = optional(list(string), ["1", "2", "3"])
  }))
```

### <a name="input_location"></a> [location](#input\_location)

Description: The Azure region in which to deploy the load balancer.

Type: `string`

### <a name="input_name"></a> [name](#input\_name)

Description: The load balancer name. Names are provided by the consumer.

Type: `string`

### <a name="input_parent_id"></a> [parent\_id](#input\_parent\_id)

Description: The fully-qualified resource ID of the existing resource group.

Type: `string`

## Optional Inputs

The following input variables are optional (have default values):

### <a name="input_backend_address_pool_addresses"></a> [backend\_address\_pool\_addresses](#input\_backend\_address\_pool\_addresses)

Description: Explicit backend members by stable key. name and backend\_address\_pool\_object\_name (pool input key) are required. Supply exactly one of ip\_address (IP mode, with optional virtual\_network\_resource\_id overriding pool/default VNet) or load\_balancer\_frontend\_ip\_configuration\_resource\_id (Frontend mode on a Global LB, referencing a public regional LB frontend). Frontend members cannot specify a VNet. A dedicated refreshing pool endpoint owns this authoritative list, including [] for last-member removal. Native NIC memberships require a separate NIC-mode pool and remain owned by the NIC owner.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name                                                = string
    backend_address_pool_object_name                    = string
    ip_address                                          = optional(string)
    virtual_network_resource_id                         = optional(string)
    load_balancer_frontend_ip_configuration_resource_id = optional(string)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_backend_address_pool_configuration"></a> [backend\_address\_pool\_configuration](#input\_backend\_address\_pool\_configuration)

Description: Default virtual network resource ID for IP-based backend pools and addresses.

Type: `string`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_backend_address_pools"></a> [backend\_address\_pools](#input\_backend\_address\_pools)

Description: Backend pools by stable input key: unique name, backend\_address\_type (NIC default for omission/null, IP, or Frontend), optional virtual\_network\_resource\_id and tunnel\_interfaces (identifier, port, protocol, type). The parent owns metadata, not member lists. NIC creates no explicit-member writer or cleanup; membership remains exclusively with the NIC owner. Opt into IP for explicit addresses. Dedicated endpoints authoritatively manage IP/Frontend members, including [] to clear the last member and fixed-empty destroy cleanup. Global pools require explicit Frontend mode and no VNet/tunnels; regional pools require IP or NIC. Modes declare ownership, not an Azure conversion: keep existing IP pools explicitly IP; clear explicit members before switching to NIC; detach native NICs before switching from NIC. Coordinate mode changes separately.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name                        = optional(string, "bepool-1")
    backend_address_type        = optional(string, "NIC")
    virtual_network_resource_id = optional(string)
    tunnel_interfaces = optional(map(object({
      identifier = number
      port       = number
      protocol   = string
      type       = string
    })), {})
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_diagnostic_settings"></a> [diagnostic\_settings](#input\_diagnostic\_settings)

Description: A map of diagnostic settings to create on the resource. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the diagnostic setting. One will be generated if not set, however this will not be unique if you want to create multiple diagnostic setting resources.
- `logs` - (Optional) A set of log entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of a specific log category to enable. Mutually exclusive with `category_group`.
  - `category_group` - (Optional) The name of a log category group to enable (for example, `allLogs` or `audit`). Mutually exclusive with `category`.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the log entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the log entry.
    - `days` - (Optional) The retention period in days. Defaults to `0` (retain indefinitely).
    - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the retention policy is enabled. Defaults to `false`.
- `metrics` - (Optional) A set of metric entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of the metric category to enable.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the metric entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the metric entry, with the same `days` and `enabled` attributes as `logs.retention_policy`.
- `log_analytics_destination_type` - (Optional) The destination type for the diagnostic setting. Possible values are `Dedicated` and `AzureDiagnostics`. Defaults to `Dedicated`.
- `workspace_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the log analytics workspace to send logs and metrics to.
- `storage_account_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the storage account to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_authorization_rule_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the event hub authorization rule to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_name` - (Optional) The name of the event hub. If none is specified, the default event hub will be selected.
- `marketplace_partner_resource_id` - (Optional) The full ARM resource ID of the Marketplace resource to which you would like to send Diagnostic Logs.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name = optional(string, null)
    logs = optional(set(object({
      category       = optional(string, null)
      category_group = optional(string, null)
      enabled        = optional(bool, true)
      retention_policy = optional(object({
        days    = optional(number, 0)
        enabled = optional(bool, false)
      }), {})
    })), [])
    metrics = optional(set(object({
      category = optional(string, null)
      enabled  = optional(bool, true)
      retention_policy = optional(object({
        days    = optional(number, 0)
        enabled = optional(bool, false)
      }), {})
    })), [])
    log_analytics_destination_type           = optional(string, "Dedicated")
    workspace_resource_id                    = optional(string, null)
    storage_account_resource_id              = optional(string, null)
    event_hub_authorization_rule_resource_id = optional(string, null)
    event_hub_name                           = optional(string, null)
    marketplace_partner_resource_id          = optional(string, null)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_ignore_body_changes"></a> [ignore\_body\_changes](#input\_ignore\_body\_changes)

Description: Body-relative dot paths to ignore. Configuration for ignored paths is not sent to Azure; changes take effect after apply.  
List indices are unsupported. All LB child collections are authoritative by default. Ignoring a collection disables management of its configured changes; do not use this to hide convergence defects.
- `network_load_balancers` - LB body paths.
- `authorization_locks` - Lock paths.
- `authorization_role_assignments` - RBAC paths.
- `insights_diagnostic_settings` - Diagnostic paths.

AzAPI 2.13 does not support ignore\_body\_changes on update\_resource or resource\_action. Dedicated member updates and fixed-empty cleanup therefore do not expose an unsupported ignore argument; their lists remain authoritative.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    network_load_balancers         = optional(list(string), [])
    authorization_locks            = optional(list(string), [])
    authorization_role_assignments = optional(list(string), [])
    insights_diagnostic_settings   = optional(list(string), [])
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_role_assignments"></a> [role\_assignments](#input\_role\_assignments)

Description: A map of role assignments to create on the load balancer. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the role assignment. If not set, a random UUID will be generated. Changing this forces the creation of a new resource.
- `role_definition_id_or_name` - The ID or name of the role definition to assign to the principal.
- `principal_id` - The ID of the principal to assign the role to.
- `description` - (Optional) The description of the role assignment.
- `skip_service_principal_aad_check` - (Optional) If set to true, skips the Azure Active Directory check for the service principal in the tenant. Defaults to false.
- `condition` - (Optional) The condition which will be used to scope the role assignment.
- `condition_version` - (Optional) The version of the condition syntax. Leave as `null` if you are not using a condition, if you are then valid values are '2.0'.
- `delegated_managed_identity_resource_id` - (Optional) The delegated Azure Resource Id which contains a Managed Identity. Changing this forces a new resource to be created. This field is only used in cross-tenant scenario.
- `principal_type` - (Optional) The type of the `principal_id`. Possible values are `User`, `Group` and `ServicePrincipal`. It is necessary to explicitly set this attribute when creating role assignments if the principal creating the assignment is constrained by ABAC rules that filters on the PrincipalType attribute.

> Note: only set `skip_service_principal_aad_check` to true if you are assigning a role to a service principal.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name                                   = optional(string, null)
    role_definition_id_or_name             = string
    principal_id                           = string
    description                            = optional(string, null)
    skip_service_principal_aad_check       = optional(bool, false)
    condition                              = optional(string, null)
    condition_version                      = optional(string, null)
    delegated_managed_identity_resource_id = optional(string, null)
    principal_type                         = optional(string, null)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

Default: `"Standard"`

### <a name="input_sku_tier"></a> [sku\_tier](#input\_sku\_tier)

Description: Regional or Global. Changing tier replaces the load balancer.

Type: `string`

Default: `"Regional"`

Description: (Optional) Tags of the resource.

Type: `map(string)`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_timeouts"></a> [timeouts](#input\_timeouts)

Description: Default per-operation timeouts applied to every `azapi` resource managed by the module. Defaults to `null` (provider defaults). Each value is a Go duration string (e.g. `30m`, `1h`).

- `create` - (Optional) Timeout for create operations.
- `read`   - (Optional) Timeout for read operations.
- `update` - (Optional) Timeout for update operations.
- `delete` - (Optional) Timeout for delete operations.

AzAPI 2.13 resource\_action executes destroy-time requests using its create timeout. Configure create for the fixed-empty member cleanup; propagation of delete alone is not a guarantee of cleanup request timeout behavior.

The stateless exact member pre-write action exposes no retry/timeouts in AzAPI 2.13 and uses its fixed 30-minute timeout. Resource retry and timeout controls do not govern that first PUT.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    create = optional(string)
    read   = optional(string)
    update = optional(string)
    delete = optional(string)
  })
```

Default: `null`
